🇲🇽🎨 "All students must have a scholarship, because they need it, because we want all of them to study." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Colima, Colima Some argue scholarships should only go to students averaging 9 or 10. She said that when she was Mexico City's head of government such a scholarship existed, and instead of motivating students it split classrooms into "good students and bad students, those who have a scholarship and those who don't." With the universal Benito Juárez scholarship for high school and Rita Cetina for secondary school, about 400,000 more young people reached high school this year. "Education is the best thing we can give our children. First comes love, and second a good education."
banner: SCHOLARSHIPS FOR ALL, NOT BY GRADES

text: 🇲🇽🎨 "A president who never gave in, who never knelt, who lived through the foreign invasion and defended the Republic." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Colima, Colima Handing out Benito Juárez scholarships in Colima, she told students why the program carries his name. When France invaded Mexico, Juárez defended the Republic as president and won; back in Mexico City he said, "Respect for the rights of others is peace." Earlier she recalled the 1846–47 US invasion that took half of Mexico's territory, and Juárez's own exile in New Orleans after Santa Anna deported him. "Many peoples of the world admire the people of Mexico because it has always fought for independence, freedom and public education."

🇲🇽✊ "Honesty is our greatest defense. The best defense of our sovereignty comes from there." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Apatzingán, Michoacán She laid out the three principles of the Fourth Transformation. "For the good of all, first the poor" is humanist thinking and an economic model: what the people pay in taxes returns to them as public works and well-being programs. "There can be no rich government with a poor people," Juárez's principle, is where moral authority comes from. And "with the people everything, without the people nothing": on the judicial reform, she asked whether it is better for judges to be chosen by a few or by the people of Mexico.

🇲🇽⚖️ "No foreign power, no elite decides over the people of Mexico. The people of Mexico hold their destiny in their own hands." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Apatzingán, Michoacán Speaking in Apatzingán days after the 212th anniversary of the 1814 Constitution of Apatzingán, she said that elsewhere in Latin America independence was led by criollo officers, sons of Spaniards with privileges, against the peninsular Spaniards. "Here in Mexico, no. It was the people who rose up in arms." She recalled Hidalgo's execution and Morelos' Sentimientos de la Nación: moderate opulence and indigence, the same education for the landowner's son as for the peon's, and "sovereignty flows from the people," today Article 39 of the Constitution.
